evidence: The hosted predicate _is_bot_authored (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:124-127) returns True only for user.type == 'Bot' or a '[bot]' login; it has no machine-user list. The engine's github.py::is_bot_author (tools/pr-approval-agent/github.py:61-64, 79-89) additionally matches _BOT_MACHINE_USERS = {'posthog-bot'} and its docstring says it 'mirrors the bot definition gating the jobs in pr-approval-agent.yml', and every Action gate enumerates posthog-bot explicitly (.github/workflows/pr-approval-agent.yml:27-30 review job, 252-255 decide-delta, 405-409 bot-author-skip). AGENTS.md:82-90 and the tasks.py:157 docstring both state the webhook pre-filter (_review_skip_reason) refuses posthog-bot; in this tree it does not. Production path for a posthog-bot PR in a default ALL-mode repo (models.py:36-43, ReviewMode.ALL default): _review_skip_reason (tasks.py:218-233) returns None (not draft; predicate false; posthog-bot is an org member so author_association is MEMBER/CONTRIBUTOR, which PAYLOAD_GATE_AUTHOR_ASSOCIATIONS admits, tasks.py:98; pr-opened.yml:115-116 confirms 'machine users like posthog-bot are' org members), the carve-out is never consulted (tasks.py:870-875), _review_mode_skip_reason returns None in ALL mode (tasks.py:274-275), and _author_lacks_write_permission passes because posthog-bot pushes snapshot commits to PR branches (ci-backend.yml:336-338). The delivery therefore creates a ReviewRun, fetch_review_context spends the PR/files/reviews/discussion/review-threads/check-runs/merged-PRs/policy calls (activities.py:211-235), a sandbox is provisioned and the PR cloned (activities.py:380, 468), review_local.py builds author_is_bot=is_bot_author(user) from the same REST user object (review_local.py:207; activities.py:248 passes 'pr' through), refuses at review_local.py:324-325 via review_pr.py:278-297, and the server then posts a public sticky comment '@posthog-bot is a bot - stamphog does not review bot-authored PRs' via _post_sticky (activities.py:758-763, 1164-1172), repeating on every synchronize. The hosted test matrix (tests/test_tasks.py:151-158) covers only user_type='Bot' and 'renovate[bot]'; the harness default is type 'User' + MEMBER (test_tasks.py:54-56), so a posthog-bot case would create a run today. Refutation checks: self-driving PRs are not misclassified - authorship is forced to the team's GitHub App machine user (tasks.py:169-171), type Bot, fixtures posthog-code[bot] (test_tasks.py:746, 916; test_integration.py:1393), which the predicate catches; posthog-bot (type User) cannot reach the inbox carve-out (tasks.py:169-172 returns empty when not bot-authored), so cluster 75's any-Bot concern is orthogonal and no approval is ever minted (engine refusal is the documented defense-in-depth layer, tasks.py:221-224). No workflow in this tree opens PRs as posthog-bot (browserslist/update-ai-costs/update-bot-ips/update-test-timing use a scheduled-actions App token, browserslist.yml:18-23), but the identity is a real org-wide PR author (engineering_analytics pull_requests.py:27; growth fixture shows login posthog-bot with type 'User').
notes: Real drift between the hosted predicate and both other layers, with a documented invariant (AGENTS.md:82-90, tasks.py:157) that is false and a concrete production cost: one sandbox plus ~8 GitHub calls and a public REFUSE sticky comment per head change of a posthog-bot PR in an ALL-mode hosted repo. Not must_fix: no security effect - the engine still refuses and no approval is posted. Would downgrade to consider if posthog-bot never opens PRs against hosted-configured repos (nothing in this tree does; it is external automation) or if LABEL mode were the only mode in use (posthog-bot cannot self-apply the trigger label). Would resolve if _is_bot_authored matched login in a machine-user set mirroring github.py::_BOT_MACHINE_USERS and the test matrix gained a ({'author_login': 'posthog-bot'}, False) case.
